## Purpose

Electrical power in the field can come from infrastructure sources (such
as outdoor or indoor outlets), portable generators, or solar power. This
SOP outlines the risks associated with using electricity in the field
and develops strategies to mitigate those risks.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Use of portable generators (Honda EU2000i and Ryobi
  RYi2200A) and extension cords for powering field equipment
- **Does not apply to:** Permanent electrical installations or solar
  panel systems (to be covered in a future SOP)
- **Location:** All EA Program field sites


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                         |
|:------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, ensure training compliance                |
| Trained Personnel | Follow this SOP, perform generator maintenance         |
| New Students      | Read and understand this SOP before operating generators; complete [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) training |


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Carbon monoxide:** Engines emit carbon monoxide. Never use a
  generator inside an enclosed area (home, garage, crawl space). Fatal
  fumes can build up even with a fan or open doors and windows. Only
  operate generators outdoors, away from open windows, vents, or doors.
- **Fire and explosion:** Gasoline and its vapors are extremely
  flammable. Allow the engine to cool at least 2 minutes before
  refueling. Always use fresh gasoline. Never operate the generator near
  combustible materials.
- **Electrical shock:** Generators produce powerful voltage. Never
  operate under wet conditions and take precautions to protect the
  generator from rain and snow.
- **Electrocution / home wiring:** Never plug a generator directly into
  a home outlet. A qualified electrician must install a Power Transfer
  Switch for any home connection.
- **Heat from cables:** Ensure cables are rated for the current being
  carried. Never leave cables coiled, as coiled cords can generate
  excessive heat.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Closed-toed shoes
- [ ] Work gloves (when handling hot engine components or refueling)
- [ ] Hearing protection (if operating near the generator for extended
      periods)

### Emergency Procedures

Use a battery-powered carbon monoxide detector in the area where you
are running a generator. If the alarm sounds, move to fresh air
immediately and shut down the generator. Refer to
[SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) for general field
emergency procedures.


## Equipment and Materials

| Item                                | Notes                                    |
|:------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Honda EU2000i generator             | Portable inverter generator              |
| Ryobi RYi2200A generator           | Portable inverter generator              |
| High-capacity extension cords      | Must be grounded type, rated for the application |
| Spare gas container                | Filled with ethanol-free gasoline        |
| Synthetic 10W-30 engine oil        | Recommended oil type for both generators |
| Funnel                             | For adding oil                           |


## Procedure

### Pre-Start Checks

1. **Check oil level.** If low, use a funnel to add synthetic 10W-30
   oil. This does not need to be done every time; check every few weeks.
   If the generator shuts off after running for about 30 minutes, low
   oil is the likely cause.

2. **Check gas level.** If low, add ethanol-free gas from the spare
   container. On the Ryobi, fill to about an inch below the top of the
   tank. Both generators can be refilled while running. The Ryobi should
   be refilled after about 4 hours of operation; the Honda after about
   6 hours.

### Starting the Honda EU2000i

1. Turn the fuel tank cap vent (black cap on top of the generator) to
   the ON position. If this is not done, the generator will shut off
   after a few minutes.
2. Make sure the eco-throttle switch (on the side panel, below the fuel
   cap vent) is OFF.
3. For a cold start, move the choke (upper left front, near the engine
   switch) to the CLOSED position (slide the switch to the right).
4. Turn the engine switch to ON.
5. Pull the starter grip quickly several times until the engine starts.
6. Allow the engine a few minutes to warm up, then slowly move the choke
   to the OPEN position.
7. **To shut down:** Turn the engine switch to OFF. After the engine has
   cooled, turn the fuel tank cap vent to OFF.

### Starting the Ryobi RYi2200A

1. Make sure the auto idle switch is OFF.
2. Move the choke to approximately halfway across. The marked cold-start
   position is slightly less than halfway, but the choke needs to go a
   bit further; you should feel a slight resistance at the correct
   position.
3. Prime the system by slowly pulling the starter grip several times.
4. Pull the grip quickly until the engine runs.
5. Allow the engine to run for 15--30 seconds, then move the choke all
   the way across to the RUN position.
6. **To shut down:** Switch the choke back to the OFF position.

### Storage

If you do not plan to use the generator within 30 days, add fuel
stabilizer to the gas and drain the carburetor.

### Extension Cord Safety

- Use only grounded extension cords rated for the intended application.
- Always uncoil cords completely and lay them flat in open locations;
  coiled cords can generate excessive heat.


## Maintenance

### General (Both Units)

Keep generators in a clean, dry environment, not exposed to dust, dirt,
moisture, or corrosive vapors. To clean, use a soft-bristle brush and/or
vacuum cleaner to loosen and remove dirt and debris. Clean air vents
with air pressure no more than 25 psi. Wipe exterior surfaces with a
damp cloth. Perform maintenance more frequently when the generator is
used in dusty areas. If you notice a power loss, the exhaust port and
muffler may be blocked with carbon deposits; allow only qualified
service technicians to clean these.

### Ryobi RYi2200A Maintenance Schedule

| Item              | Frequency                              | Notes |
|:------------------|:---------------------------------------|:------|
| Air filter        | Check before each use; clean every 3 months or 50 hours; replace every year or 300 hours | Wash with soapy water, rinse, squeeze dry |
| Engine lubricant  | Check before each use; change after first 20 hours, then every 6 months or 100 hours | Drain while warm for faster flow |
| Spark plug        | Check every 6 months or 100 hours; replace every year or 300 hours | Gap: 0.024--0.028 in (0.60--0.70 mm) |
| Spark arrestor    | Clean periodically                     | Wire brush; inspect screen for damage |
| Fuel tank / carburetor | Check fuel hose before each use; inspect fuel filter before each use; have tank and filter cleaned by qualified service center every 6 months or 100 hours | Drain both before storage to prevent gum deposits |
| Valve clearance   | Check every year or 300 hours          | Service by qualified technician |

### Honda EU2000i Maintenance Schedule

| Item              | Frequency                              | Notes |
|:------------------|:---------------------------------------|:------|
| Air filter        | Check before each use; clean every 3 months or 50 hours | Wash in detergent and warm water or non-flammable solvent; soak in clean engine oil and squeeze excess before reinstalling |
| Engine lubricant  | Check before each use; change after first 20 hours, then every 6 months or 100 hours | Fill to upper limit of oil filler neck |
| Spark plug        | Check every 6 months or 100 hours; replace every year or 200 hours | Gap: 0.024--0.028 in (0.60--0.70 mm); new plug: tighten 1/2 turn after seating; used plug: tighten 1/8--1/4 turn |
| Spark arrestor    | Clean every 6 months or 100 hours      | Wire brush; inspect screen for damage |
| Fuel tank / combustion chamber | Clean fuel tank and filter every 6 months or 100 hours; clean combustion chamber every 300 hours; check fuel line every 2 years | Service by authorized Honda dealer |
| Valve clearance   | Check every year or 200 hours          | Service by qualified technician |

## Training Record

Before operating generators independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) training
3. Review the manufacturer's operating instructions for the generator
   being used
4. Observe a trained operator start, run, and shut down the generator
5. Perform the startup and shutdown procedure under supervision
6. Be signed off by the PI or designated trainer
